claim: Chromatin boundaries subdivide eukaryotic chromosomes into functionally autonomous domains of genetic activity.
source_text: Chromatin boundaries subdivide eukaryotic chromosomes into functionally autonomous domains of genetic activity.
evidence_reasoning: This is an established concept in chromatin biology, supported by the citation to Gaszner and Felsenfeld, 2006 in the introduction.

claim: Chromatin boundaries insulate genes and/or regulatory elements within a domain from promiscuous interactions with nearby domains.
source_text: This subdivision insulates genes and/or regulatory elements within a domain from promiscuous interactions with nearby domains.
evidence_reasoning: This describes the established function of chromatin boundaries, supported by literature citations.

claim: The chromosomal domain landscape may be subject to tissue and stage specific regulation.
source_text: While it was previously assumed that the chromosomal domain landscape is fixed, there is now growing evidence that the landscape may be subject to tissue and stage specific regulation.
evidence_reasoning: This represents emerging evidence from the field, as indicated by 'growing evidence' and supported by citations in the introduction.

claim: Elba is a novel developmentally restricted boundary factor.
source_text: Here we report the isolation and characterization of a novel developmentally restricted boundary factor, Elba.
evidence_reasoning: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by experimental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: Elba is an unusual hetero-tripartite protein complex that requires all three proteins for DNA binding and insulator activity.
source_text: We show that Elba is an unusual hetero-tripartite protein complex that requires all three proteins for DNA binding and insulator activity.
evidence_reasoning: This is a primary finding demonstrated through in vitro reconstitution experiments and functional assays shown in Figures 4-6.

claim: Boundary elements have enhancer-blocking or insulator activity.
source_text: The specific functions that can be ascribed to most boundary elements include an enhancer-blocking or insulator activity
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about boundary elements, supported by multiple citations (Holdridge and Dorsett, 1991; Kellum and Schedl, 1991; Chung et al., 1993).

claim: Boundary elements have silencer-blocking or barrier activity.
source_text: The specific functions that can be ascribed to most boundary elements include...a silencer-blocking or barrier activity
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge supported by citations (Kellum and Schedl, 1991; Chung et al., 1993; Burgess–Beusse et al., 2002).

claim: Boundary elements can bring distant chromosomal DNA segments in close proximity when combined in specific pairwise combinations.
source_text: when combined in specific pairwise combinations an ability to bring distant chromosomal DNA segments in close proximity
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge supported by citations (Cai and Shen, 2001; Muravyova et al., 2001).

claim: In S. pombe, boundaries help restrict and maintain the heterochromatin state of the silenced mating type locus.
source_text: In the yeast S. pombe, boundaries help restrict and maintain the heterochromatin state of the silenced mating type locus
evidence_reasoning: This is a specific finding from another organism, supported by citation to Noma et al., 2001.

claim: In Drosophila, boundary elements play a critical role in the Bithorax complex, helping to ensure that the three BX-C homeotic genes properly specify segmental identity.
source_text: In Drosophila, boundary elements play a critical role in the Bithorax complex (BX-C), helping to ensure that the three BX-C homeotic genes properly specify segmental identity
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about Drosophila development, supported by citation to Maeda and Karch, 2006.

claim: In vertebrates, boundaries have been implicated in controlling the expression of mRNAs encoding different neuronal Protocadherin-alpha isoforms.
source_text: In vertebrates, boundaries have been implicated in controlling the expression of mRNAs encoding different neuronal Protocadherin-alpha isoforms
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from vertebrate studies, supported by citations (Guo et al., 2011; Monahan et al., 2012).

claim: In vertebrates, boundaries regulate recombination and expression of immunoglobulin light and heavy chain genes.
source_text: In vertebrates, boundaries have been implicated in...regulating recombination and expression of immunoglobulin light and heavy chain genes
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from vertebrate immunology, supported by citation to Ribeiro de Almeida et al., 2011.

claim: Proteins conferring insulating activity in flies and vertebrates like Su(Hw), BEAF, Zw5, GAGA factor and CTCF are ubiquitously expressed and seemingly functional in all cell types.
source_text: Moreover, the proteins conferring insulating activity in flies and vertebrates like Su(Hw), BEAF, Zw5, GAGA factor and CTCF are ubiquitously expressed and seemingly functional in all cell types.
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about known insulator proteins, based on prior characterization studies.

claim: Genes can be differentially regulated during normal development and differentiation by redefining their domain organization.
source_text: However recent studies argue that the domain landscape is more dynamic than previously imagined and that genes can be differentially regulated during normal development and differentiation and in the progression of disease states like cancer by redefining their domain organization
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations to Bell and Felsenfeld, 2000; Witcher and Emerson, 2009; Gomes and Espinosa, 2010.

claim: Regulation of the imprinted Igf2 and H19 genes pivots on parent of origin differences in the DNA methylation pattern and the activity of a CTCF-dependent boundary element upstream of the H19 gene.

evidence_reasoning: This is a specific example from the literature, supported by citations to Bell and Felsenfeld, 2000; Hark et al., 2000.

claim: The Fab-7 boundary can block the action of enhancers/silencers at all stages of development, apparently irrespective of tissue or cell type.
source_text: Both in the context of BX-C and in transgene assays, the Fab-7 boundary can block the action of enhancers/silencers at all stages of development, apparently irrespective of tissue or cell type
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by multiple citations (Galloni et al., 1993; Hagstrom et al., 1996; Mihaly et al., 1997; Schweinsberg et al., 2004).

claim: The Fab-7 boundary spans a sequence of 1.2 kb and consists of two prominent and one minor chromatin specific nuclease hypersensitive regions.
source_text: The Fab-7 boundary spans a sequence of 1.2 kb and consists of two prominent and one minor (*) chromatin specific nuclease hypersensitive regions (shown as yellow boxes).
evidence_reasoning: This is a structural characterization supported by experimental data and prior studies.

claim: pHS1 is a 236-bp fragment from the proximal side of HS1 which has enhancer-blocking activity only in early embryos.
source_text: pHS1 is a 236-bp fragment from the proximal side of HS1 which has enhancer-blocking activity only in early embryos

claim: The enhancer-blocking activity of pHS1 in early embryos depends upon an 8-bp sequence, CCAATAAG, called Elba.

claim: Mutations in the Elba sequence compromise the blocking activity of a 4×pHS1 multimer.
source_text: Mutations in this sequence compromise the blocking activity of a 4×pHS1 multimer

claim: Elba factor binding is detected in 0–6 hr nuclear extracts, but it is absent in 6–12 hr nuclear extracts.

claim: The constitutive insulator activity of the Fab-7 boundary is generated by sub-elements whose activity is developmentally restricted.
source_text: However, Fab-7 appears unusual in that its constitutive boundary function is generated by sub-elements whose activity is developmentally restricted.

claim: Mutations in the proximal pair of GAGA sites in HS1 weaken boundary activity in early embryos, but have little effect from mid-embryogenesis onwards.
